items.evidence: Notes cover the wheel sensor cost: "Wheel sensor cost concern raised (03:10) - Wheel sensor 50x push button cost - Budget max €12 per remote". Nothing about the components presented (chip, push buttons, wheel sensor) and nothing at all about the voice recognition chip email raised at 04:48-05:44.
The notes never mention the User Interface Designer showing existing remote controls from the web (08:34-09:29).

No statement that the new design keeps only the central buttons of the displayed models and drops the rest (08:34-09:45). "Simple remote interface confirmed (00:30)" only restates the previous meeting's recap.
"Fancy look prioritized over function (12:25) - Trend toward fruit/vegetable shapes - Spongy material trend noted". The presenter is not named, but the content matches 11:59-13:14.
"Trend toward fruit/vegetable shapes", "Spongy material trend noted", "Banana shape proposed for remote (16:30)", action item "Develop banana-shaped spongy case design".

The notes list the design points but frame them as "proposed", "debated", "questioned", "suggested"; they never say the group settled the feature list at 17:50-21:51 (standard battery, chip, odd-shaped core with spongy cover, wheel on top, buttons on the side, yellow).

Banana shape and spongy case appear ("Banana shape proposed", "Develop banana-shaped spongy case design") and lighted buttons appear ("Lighted buttons to identify side"). Missing: wheel at the top (19:34, 21:26), standard chip and standard battery (18:19-18:23, 19:22), and the voice recognition chip not being adopted.
"Industrial and UI designers to collaborate on prototype (22:55)" and "Prototype evaluation planned to check user requirements fit (22:55)" match 21:51-23:05.
Under Industrial Designer: "Collaborate with UI designer on prototype (22:44)"; under UI Designer: "Collaborate with industrial designer on prototype (22:44)".

"Prototype evaluation planned to check user requirements fit (22:55)" and the PM item "Arrange prototype development and user evaluation" match 21:51 ("evaluate the product... check if it fit the requirement given by the users").

Design points are present but presented as proposals and debates, not as a decided feature set; the 17:50-21:51 decision round (battery, chip, case, wheel position, button placement, colour) is not recorded as decided.

"Banana shape proposed for remote (16:30) - Yellow color matches company scheme" and "Develop banana-shaped spongy case design" cover the shape, colour and spongy cover, but the notes say "proposed" and "Spongy material for case questioned" rather than stating the decision taken at 17:08 ("Maybe we can keep the banana"), 19:22 ("odd shape with spongy cover") and 21:51 ("the colour is yellow").
"Lighted buttons to identify side" (under Symmetrical design), matching 20:38.

"Innovation through wheel control emphasized (14:40) - Wheel seen as easy and innovative - Potential competitive advantage" captures the reasoning, but the notes never state the decision at 15:54 ("we can keep the wheel... even if the cost is a bit higher") and 19:22 ("So we agree to put the wheel"). Instead they leave it open: "Need discussion on wheel necessity" and action items to discuss and assess the wheel sensor.
No mention of the wheel being on top of the banana (16:42, 19:34, 21:26). Only "Ergonomic curve for wheel and buttons".
No mention of the standard chip (18:23, 19:22) and no mention of voice/speech recognition at all.
No mention of the standard battery (18:19-18:22, 19:22).

errors.claim: Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested
errors.why_wrong: At 19:10 and 19:22 the Project Manager says "something odd shaped, with a spongy cover" and "odd shape with spongy cover". Nobody said heart-shaped.

errors.claim: Project Manager action item: Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity (03:30)
errors.why_wrong: The wheel question was settled in this meeting (15:54 "we can keep the wheel... even if the cost is a bit higher"; 19:22 "So we agree to put the wheel"). No further discussion was assigned to anyone.

errors.claim: Industrial Designer action item: Assess cost implications of wheel sensor (03:30)
errors.why_wrong: The Industrial Designer already reported the cost (50 times a push button) and the group decided to keep the wheel despite it. No one was asked to assess the cost further.

errors.claim: Symmetrical design for left/right hand users (19:40) - Buttons and wheel placement for ambidextrous use
errors.why_wrong: Listed under Design Decisions, but no symmetrical design was decided. The Project Manager floated symmetry at 19:52, the User Interface Designer objected that turning the remote puts the buttons on the other side, and the Project Manager closed it at 20:56 by saying users will use one hand and it "doesn't change that much". The layout decided is wheel on top, buttons on the side (21:26).
